title: Total Edge Irregularity Strength of Cubic Graphs

definitions.name: x2611_16338_vertexSum
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16338_vertexSum {V : Type*} (φ : V → ℕ) : Sym2 V → ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => φ u + φ v, fun u v => Nat.add_comm (φ u) (φ v)⟩
definitions.notes: Sum of the labels at the two endpoints of an unordered edge. Sym2.lift uses commutativity of natural addition to make the sum independent of endpoint order.

definitions.name: x2611_16338_totalLabeling
definitions.lean:
def x2611_16338_totalLabeling {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (s : ℕ)
    (φ : V → ℕ) (ψ : Sym2 V → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ v, 1 ≤ φ v ∧ φ v ≤ s) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, 1 ≤ ψ e ∧ ψ e ≤ s) ∧
  Set.InjOn (fun e => x2611_16338_vertexSum φ e + ψ e) G.edgeSet
definitions.notes: A total edge irregular s-labeling, with separate vertex and edge maps modeling their disjoint union. All vertex labels and graph-edge labels lie in [1,s], and total weights are injective on the graph’s unordered edge set. Values of ψ on nonedges are irrelevant.

definitions.name: x2611_16338_tes
definitions.notes: The least positive natural s admitting a total edge irregular s-labeling. sInf on naturals gives this minimum for finite graphs, where such labelings exist; its totalization is 0 when there is no admissible s. Only finite graphs occur in the worklist.

definitions.name: x2611_16338_edgeClass
definitions.notes: The paper’s E_r: graph edges whose two endpoint labels sum to r. Class sizes in the statements use Set.ncard; every relevant set is finite because the vertex type is finite.

statements.label: Theorem A
statements.name: x2611_16338_theorem_a
statements.original:
Every finite simple cubic graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfies

 $\operatorname{tes}(G)=\frac{n}{2}+1.$
statements.lean: (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) : x2611_16338_tes G = Fintype.card V / 2 + 1
statements.notes: Finite simple graphs are Mathlib SimpleGraph on a finite vertex type; cubic means IsRegularOfDegree 3. Natural-number division agrees with n/2 because cubic graphs have even order. No connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is added; the empty finite graph is included.

statements.label: Lemma 2.1 (Admissibility)
statements.name: x2611_16338_lemma2_1
statements.original:
Let $s\geq 3$ , and let $\varphi:V(G)\to\{1,s\}$ be a vertex labeling of a finite simple graph $G$ .
Write
 $(a,b,c)=(|E_{2}|,|E_{s+1}|,|E_{2s}|)$ .
Then, $\varphi$ extends to a total edge irregular $s$ -labeling of $G$ if and only if

 $a,b,c\leq s,\hskip 20.00003pta+b,b+c\leq 2s-1,\hskip 20.00003pta+b+c\,(={|E(G)|})\leq 3s-2.$ 

(2)

statements.notes: The three edge classes are counted as sets of unordered edges. A total labeling extending φ means an edge map ψ satisfying the registered totalLabeling predicate. Every inequality in (2), including both consecutive-pair bounds, is retained. The parenthetical equality a+b+c=|E(G)| follows from the binary-label hypothesis and s≥3.

statements.label: Section 3: edge and incidence counts
statements.name: x2611_16338_cubic_incidence_counts
statements.original:
Let $G$ be a finite simple cubic graph on $n$ vertices, and put $s=n/2+1\,(\geq 3)$ .
In view of (1), it suffices to find a total edge irregular $s$ -labeling of $G$ .

Note that the vertex labelings $\varphi:V(G)\to\{1,s\}$ are in bijection with the subsets $U$ of $V(G)$ by letting $U=\varphi^{-1}(1)$ .

Assume now that $a\,(=c)>s$ .
The average degrees of the subgraphs of $G$ induced by $U$ and $V(G)\setminus U$ are equal and are given by $\overline{d}_{U}$ , where

 $U\leftarrow(U\setminus\{u\})\cup\{v\}.$

 $a\leftarrow a-3.$
